## 2026-08-17

- Completed `RH-W-0036`: a stale generated checker no longer disables its own replacement. The replaceable-output gate conflated authenticity with freshness, so any change to `check_script()` permanently froze every installed consumer. Builder provenance plus the embedded `MANIFEST_SHA256` naming these exact manifest bytes now gates the set, and byte equality with the current template only decides whether the checker itself needs replacing. The weaker proof authorizes exactly one repair, replacing the checker itself; every other generated path still requires byte equality with the current template, so manifest digest authentication, path safety, exact projection comparison, and zero-write checking are unchanged.
- Completed `RH-W-0034`: a Spanish-only installation now passes the checker its own builder emits, because the generated `parse_manifest()` accepts exactly the locale domain `normalize_documentation_languages()` accepts instead of demanding `en` first. The Spanish documentation map advertises only destinations its render creates; the accumulating regression that proved this also exposed two unpredicted defects in bilingual mode, where the map pointed one level too high. Report-language step 3 now requires evidence the host can attribute to the human and a new step 4 asks once instead of falling back silently. A new Failure Ownership contract classifies the failing owner before any provider handoff, so a mismatch among builder-generated output never reaches provider reporting, issue creation, or repository publication. A temporary Spanish-only fixture of 33 files verified both checkers `current` with 0 writes and 0 stale, 10 resolving links, and no bilingual-only path; the external consumer was never touched.
- Completed `RH-W-0035`: the canonical suite spawned a bare `python` in 13 subprocess calls while already using `sys.executable` in 9 others, so it could not start where PATH has no `python`, and generated consumer text named `python .repo-harness/check.py` while the generated checker carried a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang. Every bare literal is now `sys.executable`, one guard scans each test module for interpreter-name constants, generated copy names both the Windows and POSIX cases, and the POSIX-only inline environment assignment in `references/validation.md` is split per shell. A blanket `python3` substitution was rejected because `python3` is absent from a default python.org Windows installation; platform-conditional rendering was rejected because the generated file is committed into a repository that contributors on the other systems clone. Real macOS and Linux execution remains unverified for lack of hardware.
